reason: The wound needs clearing, and the picture shows phagocytes engulfing debris near the cut.
expectation: The phagocytes should help clear debris from the wound.

effect: Debris is cleared, and the wound now has supply, surface and support slots to fill.
reaction: The named slots make the remaining repair jobs clearer.
reason: The repair signals point to the nearby vessel, suggesting they help establish the wound's blood supply.
expectation: The signals should help the nearby capillary supply the healing wound.

effect: The signals produced a vessel branch connected to the existing circulation, which looks suitable for the wound's supply slot.
reaction: The connection to the original capillary makes the new supply easier to understand.
reason: The capillary sprout appears to fit the healing body's supply slot.
expectation: The sprout should supply the healing wound.

effect: The capillary sprout fills the supply slot and forms a connected route that brings nutrients to the wound.
reaction: The completed loop makes the supply route clear.
reason: The fibroblast picture shows a collagen gene, and the RNA building blocks are arriving in its nucleus. This looks like a step toward making wound support.
expectation: The fibroblasts should make an RNA message for collagen.

effect: The fibroblasts now have an RNA copy of the collagen instructions, ready at the ribosomes.
reaction: It connects the earlier protein-making steps to wound repair.
reason: Matrix nutrients include amino acids, which the fibroblasts can use to make collagen from the message.
expectation: The fibroblasts should make collagen to support the wound.

effect: The fibroblasts used the message and nutrients to make collagen fibres in the damaged dermis, producing new connective tissue.
reaction: It is useful to see how the collagen ends up outside the cells.
reason: The new connective tissue looks like it can fill the wound's support slot.
expectation: The connective tissue should support the healing wound.

effect: The new connective tissue fills the support slot, though it is not yet as strong as uninjured skin.
reaction: The distinction between new and uninjured tissue is useful.
reason: The surface still needs closing, and nutrients arrive beneath the epidermal edge cells.
expectation: The nourished edge cells should help form a new surface over the wound.

effect: The edge cells formed a new surface across the gap, ready for the remaining surface slot.
reaction: It is clear how the wound can close from its edges.
reason: The new surface fits the healing body's remaining surface slot.

choice.combine: Body with healing skin[Capillary sprout,New connective tissue]

expectation: The new surface should close the wound over the supported tissue.

effect: The new surface closes the gap, completing the wound's surface, support and supply goal; the temporary clot still needs clearing.
reaction: It is useful to see that the surface can close before the deeper tissue regains strength.
reason: The clot-clearing enzymes are shown breaking down fibrin, which reinforced the temporary clot.

choice.combine: Body with healing skin[Capillary sprout,New connective tissue,New surface]

expectation: The enzymes should clear the temporary fibrin clot.

effect: The enzymes cleared most of the temporary fibrin, completing the goals; the closed skin still has a maturing scar.
reaction: It was useful to see that repair continues after the clot is cleared.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making collagen support was most worthwhile: it connected a DNA instruction to an RNA message, protein-making and fibres outside the cell.

leastWorthwhile.text: Slotting the finished surface into the body felt mostly like confirming a predictable result after the cells had already crossed the gap.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the surface could close while the deeper tissue was still gaining strength.

arbitrary.text: The surface slotting felt a little mechanical, although its purpose was clear; nothing else stood out as purposeless.

continue.text: I would choose to continue if another chapter connected familiar cell processes to a new body problem as clearly as the collagen repair did.
